text: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the reports about Jesus,
and he said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist. He has been raised from the dead, and that is why these miraculous powers are at work in him."

versions.text: and he said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist. He has been raised from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work in him."
versions.explanation: αἱ δυνάμεις here denotes miracle-working powers. The bare word "powers" is ambiguous in English (it can suggest spiritual beings); adding "miraculous" clarifies the sense for a listening audience.

text: For Herod had arrested John, bound him, and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip,
since John had been telling him, "It is not lawful for you to have her."
Herod wanted to kill him, but he was afraid of the crowd, because they regarded John as a prophet.
On Herod's birthday the daughter of Herodias danced before the guests and pleased Herod so much
that he swore an oath to give her whatever she asked.
Prompted by her mother, she said, "Give me the head of John the Baptist here on a platter."
The king was distressed, but because of his oaths and his guests he ordered that it be given to her.
He sent word and had John beheaded in the prison.
His head was brought in on a platter and given to the girl, and she took it to her mother.
Then John's disciples came, took the body, and buried him; and they went and told Jesus.

versions.text: Then John's disciples came, took the body, and buried it; and they went and told Jesus.
versions.explanation: The Greek pronoun is masculine (αὐτόν), "buried him," which preserves the personal reference to John rather than reducing him to "it."

text: When Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there by boat to a deserted place, to be alone. But the crowds heard of it and followed him on foot from the towns.
When he came ashore, he saw a large crowd, and he had compassion on them and healed their sick.

versions.text: When he came ashore, he saw the great crowd, and he had compassion on them and healed their sick.
versions.explanation: πολὺν ὄχλον is anarthrous — "a large crowd." The definite "the great crowd" implies a crowd already specified and overstates the Greek.

text: As evening drew on, the disciples came to him and said, "This is a deserted place, and the hour is already late. Send the crowds away, so they can go to the villages and buy food for themselves."
But Jesus said to them, "They do not need to go away. You give them something to eat."
"We have nothing here," they said, "except five loaves and two fish."
"Bring them here to me," he said.

He ordered the crowds to sit down on the grass. Then he took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, gave thanks, and broke the loaves. He gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.
They all ate and were satisfied, and they gathered up twelve baskets full of the leftover pieces.
Those who ate numbered about five thousand men, besides women and children.
Immediately he made the disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of him to the other side, while he dismissed the crowds.
After sending them away, he went up on the mountain by himself to pray. When evening came, he was there alone,
while the boat was already a long way from land, battered by the waves, for the wind was against them.

versions.text: while the boat was already many stadia from land, battered by the waves, for the wind was against them.
versions.explanation: "Stadia" is an unfamiliar unit for listeners and interrupts the flow of oral reading. A distance expression conveys the sense; a footnote could note "Greek: many stadia; a stadion was about 180 meters."

text: In the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea.
When the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were terrified. "It's a ghost!" they said, and they cried out in fear.
But at once Jesus spoke to them: "Take heart, it is I. Do not be afraid."
Peter answered him, "Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the water."
"Come," he said. So Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came to Jesus.

versions.text: "Come," he said. So Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.
versions.explanation: πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν with ἦλθεν means he actually came to Jesus; "toward" weakens the statement and suggests he did not arrive.

text: But when he saw how strong the wind was, he was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out, "Lord, save me!"
At once Jesus reached out his hand and caught hold of him. "You of little faith," he said, "why did you doubt?"
And when they had climbed into the boat, the wind died down.
Then those in the boat worshiped him, saying, "Truly you are the Son of God."
When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret.
And when the men of that place recognized him, they sent word throughout the whole surrounding region, and people brought him all who were sick.
They begged him to let them merely touch the fringe of his cloak, and all who touched it were healed.
